Estamos planificando (NO implementando todavía — modo plan de solo lectura) recrear el backend de este proyecto en NestJS, como servicio nuevo que convive en paralelo con el backend Python/FastAPI existente (sin tocarlo ni el docker-compose actual de frontend+backend, hasta que se decida el corte más adelante).

## Contexto del repo (ruta: /home/adrian/projects/frontend)

**Backend Python actual** (`backend/main.py`, FastAPI, stateless, sin persistencia):
- `POST /find-communities`: recibe un `Startup` (name, description, target_customer, stage, category — todos strings/enums sueltos, sin persistir), llama a OpenAI (gpt-4o) con el catálogo `backend/communities.json` (lista estática de comunidades: id, name, platform, size, tags, categories, engagement) y pide que rankee las 10 mejores devolviendo relevance_score, icp_match, engagement_level, time_to_first_customer por comunidad.
- `POST /generate-playbook`: recibe startup + community_name/platform/description, llama a OpenAI para generar un playbook (week1_actions, kpis, dos/donts, first_post {title, body, post_type}, first_dm_template, insider_tip). No persiste nada.
- `GET /dashboard-stats`: devuelve stats hardcodeadas (communities_mapped, startups_helped, avg_days_to_first_customer).
- Ya tiene Dockerfile (Debian: `caddy:2` multi-stage + `python:3.12-slim-bookworm`, Caddy reverse-proxeando a uvicorn dentro del mismo contenedor) — patrón ya establecido y funcionando, ver `backend/Dockerfile`, `backend/Caddyfile`, `backend/entrypoint.sh`.
- `backend/.env` tiene una `OPENAI_API_KEY` real ya configurada.

**Frontend** (`frontend/index.html`, `frontend/map.html`, estático, servido por Caddy): llama a `API_BASE = '/api'` → `/api/find-communities`, `/api/generate-playbook`, `/api/dashboard-stats`. NO debe tocarse en este trabajo (el nuevo backend NestJS no se conecta al frontend todavía).

**docker-compose.yml** (raíz): actualmente define `backend` (Python) y `frontend` (Caddy), con la cadena frontend-Caddy → backend-Caddy → uvicorn ya verificada funcionando end-to-end. NO modificar estos dos servicios; el backend NestJS se añade como servicio(s) adicionales e independientes (puerto propio, ej. 8081), sin wiring al proxy `/api` del frontend.

**Dos documentos de especificación que el usuario dio como fuente de verdad, y que confirmó representan "la misma idea de negocio" (pidió que se reconcilien en un solo modelo, no elegir uno u otro):**

1. `docs/launchmap-domain-model.mmd` (diagrama de clases Mermaid, solo en disco local, nunca commiteado a git) — modelo de dominio actual/aspiracional:
   - `Startup` (id, pitch: StartupPitch{name, description, target_customer}, stage: Stage enum{IDEA, PRE_LAUNCH, LAUNCHED, GROWING}, category: Category enum{HEALTHTECH, B2B_SAAS, FINTECH, EDTECH, DEVELOPER_TOOLS, AI, GENERAL_STARTUP})
   - `MatchResult` (id, startup_id, matches: 1..10 CommunityMatch, computed_at, método top(n)) *-- `CommunityMatch` (community_id, relevance: RelevanceScore{value}, icp_match, engagement: EngagementLevel enum{LOW,MEDIUM,HIGH,VERY_HIGH}, time_to_first_customer)
   - `Playbook` (id, startup_id, community_id, week1_actions, first_post: FirstPost{title,body,post_type}, dm_template, outcome: Outcome{status: OutcomeStatus enum{NOT_EXECUTED,EXECUTED,CONVERTED,NO_RESPONSE}, replies, dms, signups, recorded_at}, método record_outcome(status))
   - Interfaces explícitas de repositorio: `PlaybookRepository{find_by_id, save}`, `MatchResultRepository{find_by_id, save}`, `CommunityMatcher{match(startup, catalog)}` — es decir, el diagrama pide explícitamente arquitectura con puertos/interfaces de repositorio, no acceso directo a ORM desde los servicios.

2. `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` (raíz, sí está en git) — producto renombrado "Chick", con flujo de 5 pasos y modelo de datos:
   - `Brief` (id, raw_input, product_summary, audience_segments: array de strings, stage: enum{idea, mvp, early-traction}, created_at) — paso 1: intake en lenguaje natural + pregunta de aclaración + resumen editable en chips.
   - `Result` (id, brief_id, channel_type: enum{discord, reddit, facebook_group, company, individual}, name, url, why_it_fits, reach_score (1-5), receptiveness_score (1-5), warmth_score (1-5), confidence_total (computado), source: enum{verified_data, web_search, manual}, suggested_approach, draft_message) — pasos 2-4: discovery + scoring + estrategia/outreach.
   - Fórmula de scoring (v1, basada en reglas, NO ML): `confidence_total = reach_score*0.3 + receptiveness_score*0.4 + warmth_score*0.3` (receptiveness pesa más porque un canal de mucho alcance pero baja receptividad puede quemar la relación/cuenta).
   - `Attempt` (id, result_id, message_sent, outcome: enum{no_response, declined, interested, signed_up, paying}, revenue (opcional, solo si paying), notes, logged_at) — paso 5: tracking, los outcomes retroalimentan el scoring futuro (closed loop, es el diferenciador core del producto, no un nice-to-have).
   - Dashboard/tracking view (una vez hay attempts logueados): KPIs (total attempts, response rate, sign-ups, revenue), growth over time, funnel (attempts → interested → signed_up → paying con drop-off), performance por channel_type, log de attempts recientes, y un "refinement insight" en lenguaje plano generado solo cuando hay 3+ attempts logueados (ej. "communities are converting at X% vs Y% for cold email").
   - Fuera de alcance para MVP: descubrimiento por ubicación física/eventos, Instagram, aprendizaje de patrones cross-usuario, re-scraping continuo, intake por voz.

También existe `prototype/chick-tech-arch.html` (doc de arquitectura de hackathon, NO commiteado a git, solo en disco) que sugiere Node.js+Express+Prisma+Postgres y menciona servicios externos ficticios "Fastino" (extracción texto→JSON para el intake) y "Cala" (búsqueda de conocimiento/datos de comunidades verificados) — **estos servicios NO existen, no hay credenciales ni SDKs para ellos en el repo**. La decisión ya tomada es: NO integrar Fastino/Cala; se sustituye por llamadas a OpenAI (mismo patrón que ya usa `backend/main.py`, reutilizando `OPENAI_API_KEY`) tanto para la extracción de intake (Brief) como para el matching/scoring de discovery (Result) y la generación de outreach (draft_message / kit).

## Decisiones ya confirmadas por el usuario (no volver a preguntar esto):
1. Reconciliar ambos documentos en UN solo modelo de dominio para NestJS — no elegir entre mmd y PRODUCT_SPEC.md, sino diseñar una estructura unificada que satisfaga ambos (nombres/entidades pueden tomarse de PRODUCT_SPEC.md ya que es el spec de producto "oficial" con user stories/AC, pero incorporando los patrones de arquitectura explícitos del mmd: value objects, enums, y sobre todo interfaces de repositorio/puerto en vez de acceso directo a ORM).
2. Sí añadir persistencia real (base de datos) — necesaria para Attempt/Outcome logging y el dashboard de tracking que ambos specs piden.
3. El backend NestJS convive en paralelo con el Python (nueva carpeta, ej. `backend-nest/`, servicio(s) nuevo(s) en docker-compose con puerto propio, sin tocar el flujo `/api` del frontend ni el backend Python existentes).

## Lo que necesito que diseñes (plan detallado, no código):

1. **Modelo de dominio unificado** — nombres de entidades definitivos (recomendación: usar Brief/Result/Attempt de PRODUCT_SPEC.md como entidades principales, pero decide tú si conviene mantener también Startup-style value objects tipo Category/Stage enums del mmd dentro de Brief, o si esos quedan absorbidos en `audience_segments`/`product_summary`). Define campos finales de cada entidad, cómo se calcula `confidence_total`, y cómo el patrón repository-interface del mmd (`PlaybookRepository`, `MatchResultRepository`, `CommunityMatcher`) se traduce a NestJS (tokens de inyección + interfaces TypeScript + implementación TypeORM).

2. **Stack técnico concreto para backend-nest/**: NestJS version, ORM (TypeORM recomendado por encajar mejor con el patrón repository/interface que pide el mmd, pero evalúa si Prisma sería mejor y justifica), motor de base de datos (Postgres recomendado, imagen Docker Debian — verificar que la imagen oficial de postgres usada sea la variante Debian, no alpine, consistente con la convención ya establecida en este proyecto de "usar versiones Debian" en todos los Dockerfiles), validación (class-validator/class-transformer o Zod), cliente OpenAI para Node.

3. **Estructura de módulos NestJse**: qué módulos/controllers/services/entities crear (ej. BriefModule, DiscoveryModule o ResultModule, AttemptModule, DashboardModule), y cómo se seedea el catálogo de comunidades (migrar `backend/communities.json` a una tabla/seed en la nueva base de datos, ya que PRODUCT_SPEC pide "datos verificados/sourced" pero no hay integración real disponible — usar el catálogo estático existente como fuente, dejarlo explícito como limitación conocida).

4. **Endpoints necesarios** para cubrir el flujo de 5 pasos de PRODUCT_SPEC.md + las operaciones del mmd (create Brief, discovery/matching → generar Result(s) con scoring, generar draft_message/outreach kit, log de Attempt con outcome, endpoint(s) de dashboard agregando KPIs/funnel/performance-por-canal/refinement-insight).

5. **Dockerfile Debian para backend-nest/** siguiendo el mismo patrón ya usado en `backend/Dockerfile` (multi-stage, base Debian — ej. `node:20-bookworm-slim`, no alpine) y cómo se añade a `docker-compose.yml` como servicio(s) nuevo(s) (incluyendo el servicio de Postgres) sin romper los servicios `frontend`/`backend` existentes.

6. **Plan de verificación end-to-end**: cómo levantar el nuevo servicio (docker compose build/up del nuevo servicio), y una secuencia de llamadas curl que recorra el flujo completo (crear Brief → obtener Results rankeados → generar draft de outreach → loguear un Attempt con outcome → consultar dashboard y ver que las métricas reflejan el Attempt logueado), sin depender de que el frontend ni el backend Python se toquen.

Entrega un plan de implementación detallado, con nombres de archivos concretos a crear dentro de `backend-nest/`, sin escribir el código completo (fragmentos ilustrativos ok si ayudan a fijar la interfaz, pero el foco es la estructura y las decisiones de diseño).

1	# Chick — product spec
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Chick is a GTM discovery tool for early-stage founders. Most tools in this space (Apollo, Clay, Apify, etc.) assume the user already knows their ideal customer profile. Early-stage founders don't — they have a hunch, not a confirmed audience. Chick is built for that earlier, uncertain stage: it takes a rough idea, finds real communities, companies, and people worth talking to first, ranks them by how likely they are to actually respond, and gets sharper with every outreach attempt logged.
6	
7	**One-line pitch:** Before you have an ICP, you have a hunch — Chick finds out where it lives.
8	
9	## The core insight
10	
11	Founders trying to validate an idea don't fail because the data they can access is wrong. Apollo, Clay, and Apify all work fine — the problem is they're built for a later stage, when you already know who you're looking for. Pre-validation, that confidence doesn't exist yet, so every search comes back too broad, and founders end up manually stitching together vague database searches, scraping, and scrolling communities by hand with no coherent strategy and nothing tracked. Chick's job is to be the tool for that specific, underserved stage.
12	
13	## Target user
14	
15	Pre-seed and early-stage founders, indie hackers, hackathon builders, first-time founders — anyone who needs to find and validate with real early users before they have a confirmed target customer profile.
16	
17	## Core product flow
18	
19	### Step 1 — Tell us
20	User describes their idea in plain language, not a form. The AI asks one sharpening follow-up question, then shows a structured summary back (audience segment, product type, stage) as editable chips so the user can correct anything before proceeding. This confirmation step matters — it's the moment that separates Chick from tools that assume a confident, already-correct input.
21	
22	### Step 2 — We look (discovery)
23	Based on the confirmed brief, the tool searches for real Discord servers, subreddits, Facebook groups, companies, and individuals that match each audience segment. Company/entity data should come from verified, sourced data rather than model-generated guesses.
24	
25	### Step 3 — Confidence scoring
26	Every result is scored on three axes:
27	- **Reach** — how many relevant people are actually there
28	- **Receptiveness** — will this space welcome outreach, or penalize/ban it
29	- **Warmth** — cold list vs. some existing foothold or context
30	
31	Results are sorted by a weighted combination of these three, with the top result visually flagged as the "best shot." Every result should show a one-line "why this fits" reasoning, not just a name.
32	
33	### Step 4 — Strategy and outreach
34	For the selected result, the tool recommends the specific right approach for that channel (comment first vs. direct DM vs. open post) and drafts a ready-to-edit outreach message matching that approach and channel norms.
35	
36	### Step 5 — Tracking and refinement
37	Every outreach attempt gets logged: channel, message used, and outcome (no response / declined / interested / signed up / paying customer, with an optional revenue amount for paying outcomes). Outcomes feed back into the confidence scoring model so future recommendations improve — this closed loop is the product's core differentiator, not a nice-to-have.
38	
39	## Data model
40	
41	```
42	Brief
43	- id
44	- raw_input (string, the user's original description)
45	- product_summary (string, extracted)
46	- audience_segments (array of strings)
47	- stage (enum: idea | mvp | early-traction)
48	- created_at
49	
50	Result
51	- id
52	- brief_id (fk)
53	- channel_type (enum: discord | reddit | facebook_group | company | individual)
54	- name (string)
55	- url
56	- why_it_fits (string, one-line reasoning)
57	- reach_score (1-5)
58	- receptiveness_score (1-5)
59	- warmth_score (1-5)
60	- confidence_total (computed, weighted sum of the three)
61	- source (enum: verified_data | web_search | manual)
62	- suggested_approach (string)
63	- draft_message (string)
64	
65	Attempt
66	- id
67	- result_id (fk)
68	- message_sent (string, editable copy of the draft)
69	- outcome (enum: no_response | declined | interested | signed_up | paying)
70	- revenue (number, optional, only relevant for paying outcome)
71	- notes (string, optional)
72	- logged_at
73	```
74	
75	## Scoring logic (v1, rule-based — not ML)
76	
77	```
78	confidence_total = (reach_score * 0.3) + (receptiveness_score * 0.4) + (warmth_score * 0.3)
79	```
80	
81	Receptiveness is weighted highest because a high-reach, low-receptiveness channel (e.g. posting cold in a subreddit that bans self-promotion) actively wastes the attempt and can burn the account/community relationship — the cost of a wrong approach is higher than the cost of a missed high-reach opportunity.
82	
83	## Dashboard / tracking view
84	
85	Once attempts are logged, the dashboard shows:
86	- **KPIs** — total attempts, response rate, sign-ups, revenue
87	- **Growth over time** — sign-ups and revenue trend
88	- **Funnel** — attempts → interested → signed up → paying, showing drop-off at each stage
89	- **Performance by channel type** — attempts, response rate, sign-ups, and revenue broken out by community / company / individual
90	- **Recent attempts log** — full history, most recent first
91	- **Refinement insight** — a plain-language summary of what's working (e.g. "communities are converting at X% vs Y% for cold email — future suggestions are weighted toward communities"), generated once there's enough logged data (3+ attempts minimum)
92	
93	## Out of scope for MVP (roadmap only)
94	
95	- Physical location / event discovery
96	- Instagram-specific community discovery beyond general search
97	- Cross-user aggregated pattern learning (the long-term data moat — requires real usage volume)
98	- Continuous re-scraping / live activity monitoring of discovered channels
99	- Voice-based intake
100	
101	## Brand and design reference
102	
103	- **Palette:** warm plaster background (`#F5EFE5`), terracotta accent (`#C15F3C`), deep rust (`#8E3E27`), muted olive as a rare third accent (`#767B54`), warm brown-black ink for text (`#2E241A`) — no pure black, no cold grays
104	- **Typography:** Fraunces (serif, display) paired with Work Sans (body/UI)
105	- **Tone:** grounded, plain-spoken, no corporate SaaS jargon ("leverage," "unlock," "seamless")
106	- Full landing page and interactive app prototype exist as reference HTML builds — see `/design` if included in this repo, or request from [team member] if not yet added.
107	
108	## Why this matters (for pitch reference)
109	
110	CB Insights' analysis of startup failures found that lack of market need/validation is the single leading cause of failure. Roughly 137,000 startups are created daily worldwide (Global Entrepreneurship Monitor), and the vast majority never systematically validate before building further. Existing sales intelligence tools (a market sized at $5.37B in 2026, headed toward $12.45B by 2034) are built for teams that already know their ICP — none serve the earlier, uncertain validation stage that Chick targets.

- reach_score (1-5)
- receptiveness_score (1-5)
- warmth_score (1-5)
- confidence_total (computed, weighted sum of the three)
- source (enum: verified_data | web_search | manual)
- suggested_approach (string)
- draft_message (string)

Attempt
- id
- result_id (fk)
- message_sent (string, editable copy of the draft)
- outcome (enum: no_response | declined | interested | signed_up | paying)
- revenue (number, optional, only relevant for paying outcome)
- notes (string, optional)
- logged_at
```

## Scoring logic (v1, rule-based — not ML)

```
confidence_total = (reach_score * 0.3) + (receptiveness_score * 0.4) + (warmth_score * 0.3)
```

Receptiveness is weighted highest because a high-reach, low-receptiveness channel (e.g. posting cold in a subreddit that bans self-promotion) actively wastes the attempt and can burn the account/community relationship — the cost of a wrong approach is higher than the cost of a missed high-reach opportunity.

## Dashboard / tracking view

Once attempts are logged, the dashboard shows:
- **KPIs** — total attempts, response rate, sign-ups, revenue
- **Growth over time** — sign-ups and revenue trend
- **Funnel** — attempts → interested → signed up → paying, showing drop-off at each stage
- **Performance by channel type** — attempts, response rate, sign-ups, and revenue broken out by community / company / individual
- **Recent attempts log** — full history, most recent first
- **Refinement insight** — a plain-language summary of what's working (e.g. "communities are converting at X% vs Y% for cold email — future suggestions are weighted toward communities"), generated once there's enough logged data (3+ attempts minimum)

## Out of scope for MVP (roadmap only)

- Physical location / event discovery
- Instagram-specific community discovery beyond general search
- Cross-user aggregated pattern learning (the long-term data moat — requires real usage volume)
- Continuous re-scraping / live activity monitoring of discovered channels
- Voice-based intake

## Brand and design reference

- **Palette:** warm plaster background (`#F5EFE5`), terracotta accent (`#C15F3C`), deep rust (`#8E3E27`), muted olive as a rare third accent (`#767B54`), warm brown-black ink for text (`#2E241A`) — no pure black, no cold grays
- **Typography:** Fraunces (serif, display) paired with Work Sans (body/UI)
- **Tone:** grounded, plain-spoken, no corporate SaaS jargon ("leverage," "unlock," "seamless")
- Full landing page and interactive app prototype exist as reference HTML builds — see `/design` if included in this repo, or request from [team member] if not yet added.

## Why this matters (for pitch reference)

CB Insights' analysis of startup failures found that lack of market need/validation is the single leading cause of failure. Roughly 137,000 startups are created daily worldwide (Global Entrepreneurship Monitor), and the vast majority never systematically validate before building further. Existing sales intelligence tools (a market sized at $5.37B in 2026, headed toward $12.45B by 2034) are built for teams that already know their ICP — none serve the earlier, uncertain validation stage that Chick targets.

# Plan: `backend-nest/` — servicio NestJS en paralelo al backend Python

## 0. Resumen de la decisión de reconciliación de modelos

Uso **PRODUCT_SPEC.md como fuente de nombres de entidades** (`Brief`, `Result`, `Attempt`) porque es el documento versionado en git con AC de producto, pero incorporo del `.mmd` los tres patrones arquitectónicos explícitos que pide:

1. **Value objects para campos compuestos** (no solo strings sueltos) — ej. `ScoreBreakdown` como VO en vez de tres columnas sueltas sin cohesión.
2. **Enums TypeScript reales** para todo campo cerrado (`Stage`, `ChannelType`, `Outcome`, `Source`), igual que el `.mmd` usa `Stage`/`Category`/`EngagementLevel`/`OutcomeStatus` como enums de primera clase.
3. **Interfaces de repositorio explícitas** (`BriefRepository`, `DiscoveryRepository`/`ResultRepository`, `AttemptRepository`, `ChannelMatcher`) inyectadas por token, con la implementación TypeORM detrás — esto traduce directamente `PlaybookRepository`/`MatchResultRepository`/`CommunityMatcher` del `.mmd`.

`Category` del `.mmd` (HEALTHTECH, B2B_SAAS, FINTECH, EDTECH, DEVELOPER_TOOLS, AI, GENERAL_STARTUP) **no se mantiene como enum rígido**: PRODUCT_SPEC.md pide `audience_segments` como array de strings libres extraídos por IA del texto natural del founder (más fiel al "no soy Apollo, no asumo ICP confirmado" que es el core insight del producto). Se pierde tipado fuerte de categoría, pero se gana fidelidad al spec oficial — trade-off explícito documentado en el modelo. `Stage` sí se mantiene como enum (`idea | mvp | early-traction`, valores de PRODUCT_SPEC, no los 4 del `.mmd` que son de otro naming más viejo del producto).

`Playbook`/`MatchResult` del `.mmd` colapsan en `Result` de PRODUCT_SPEC (que ya incluye score + `suggested_approach` + `draft_message` en una sola entidad, en vez de separar matching y playbook en dos tablas). `Outcome`/`OutcomeStatus` del `.mmd` se traducen a `Attempt.outcome` (enum `no_response|declined|interested|signed_up|paying`, con `revenue` opcional) — más rico que el `OutcomeStatus` de 4 valores del `.mmd` porque el spec de producto pide el funnel completo.

## 1. Modelo de dominio final

### `Brief`
```
id: uuid
raw_input: text
product_summary: text          // extraído por IA
audience_segments: string[]    // extraído por IA (jsonb column)
stage: Stage enum (idea | mvp | early_traction)
created_at: timestamptz
```

### `Result`
```
id: uuid
brief_id: fk -> Brief
channel_type: ChannelType enum (discord | reddit | facebook_group | company | individual)
name: string
url: string | null
why_it_fits: text
reach_score: int (1-5)
receptiveness_score: int (1-5)
warmth_score: int (1-5)
confidence_total: numeric(4,2)   // persistido, no derivado en query — ver más abajo
source: ResultSource enum (verified_data | web_search | manual)
suggested_approach: text | null
draft_message: text | null
created_at: timestamptz
```

`confidence_total` se calcula server-side en el momento de creación/actualización del `Result` (no como columna generada de Postgres, para poder recalcularse cuando el "refinement loop" ajuste pesos en el futuro sin migración de esquema):

```
confidence_total = reach_score*0.3 + receptiveness_score*0.4 + warmth_score*0.3
```

Esta fórmula vive en **un único lugar**: `ScoringService.computeConfidence(scores: ScoreBreakdown): number`, un value object puro (sin dependencias de NestJS/DB) para que sea trivial testear con Jest y reemplazar cuando llegue el "refinement" real basado en `Attempt` histórico.

### `Attempt`
```
id: uuid
result_id: fk -> Result
message_sent: text
outcome: AttemptOutcome enum (no_response | declined | interested | signed_up | paying)
revenue: numeric(10,2) | null   // solo relevante si outcome = paying, validado en DTO
notes: text | null
logged_at: timestamptz
```

### Traducción del patrón repository-interface del `.mmd` a NestJS

El `.mmd` pide interfaces explícitas (`PlaybookRepository`, `MatchResultRepository`, `CommunityMatcher`) en vez de acceso directo a ORM desde los servicios. En NestJS esto se hace con **tokens de inyección + interfaces TS + adaptador TypeORM**, patrón puertos-y-adaptadores:

```typescript
// domain/ports/brief.repository.ts
export interface BriefRepository {
  findById(id: string): Promise<Brief | null>;
  save(brief: Brief): Promise<Brief>;
}
export const BRIEF_REPOSITORY = Symbol('BRIEF_REPOSITORY');

// domain/ports/result.repository.ts
export interface ResultRepository {
  findById(id: string): Promise<Result | null>;
  findByBriefId(briefId: string): Promise<Result[]>;
  saveMany(results: Result[]): Promise<Result[]>;
}
export const RESULT_REPOSITORY = Symbol('RESULT_REPOSITORY');

// domain/ports/attempt.repository.ts
export interface AttemptRepository {
  save(attempt: Attempt): Promise<Attempt>;
  findAll(): Promise<Attempt[]>;         // usado por DashboardService
  findByResultId(resultId: string): Promise<Attempt[]>;
}
export const ATTEMPT_REPOSITORY = Symbol('ATTEMPT_REPOSITORY');

// domain/ports/channel-matcher.ts  (equivalente a CommunityMatcher del .mmd)
export interface ChannelMatcher {
  match(brief: Brief, catalog: ChannelCandidate[]): Promise<ScoredCandidate[]>;
}
export const CHANNEL_MATCHER = Symbol('CHANNEL_MATCHER');
```

Los adaptadores TypeORM (`TypeOrmBriefRepository`, `TypeOrmResultRepository`, `TypeOrmAttemptRepository`) implementan estas interfaces y se registran así en cada módulo:

```typescript
providers: [
  { provide: BRIEF_REPOSITORY, useClass: TypeOrmBriefRepository },
]
```

`OpenAiChannelMatcher implements ChannelMatcher` es el único punto donde se llama a OpenAI para discovery+scoring — reemplaza el "Cala" ficticio del prototipo. Los servicios de aplicación (`BriefService`, `DiscoveryService`, etc.) **solo dependen de las interfaces**, nunca de `Repository<Entity>` de TypeORM directamente ni del SDK de OpenAI directamente. Esto es justo lo que pide el `.mmd` y además hace testeable cada servicio con mocks triviales.

## 2. Stack técnico

| Decisión | Elección | Justificación |
|---|---|---|
| NestJS | `^10.x` (última estable a la fecha) | LTS de Node 20 compatible, `@nestjs/cli` para scaffolding |
| ORM | **TypeORM** (no Prisma) | El patrón repository-interface del `.mmd` encaja de forma nativa con `Repository<T>` de TypeORM inyectado dentro de un adaptador; Prisma genera un cliente global tipado que empuja hacia acceso directo desde servicios y hace más forzado ocultarlo detrás de una interfaz de dominio propia. TypeORM además tiene decoradores de entidad que mapean 1:1 con las clases del `.mmd` (`@Entity`, `@Column`, enums nativos de Postgres vía `enum:` en la columna). |
| Base de datos | **PostgreSQL** | El prototipo (`REDACTED-tech-arch.html`) ya la sugiere, y el dashboard con funnel/agregaciones se beneficia de SQL real. Imagen Docker: **`postgres:16-bookworm`** (variante Debian explícita, no `postgres:16-alpine` ni el tag `postgres:16` a secas que en Docker Hub apunta a Debian pero sin dejarlo explícito) — consistente con el patrón de comentarios explícitos ya usado en `backend/Dockerfile` y `frontend/Dockerfile` ("X es Debian-based, no alpine"). |
| Validación | **class-validator + class-transformer** | Es el paquete estándar/first-party de Nest (`ValidationPipe` global), se integra directo con DTOs decorados, evita añadir una dependencia de validación paralela (Zod) cuando Nest ya trae su propio patrón idiomático. |
| Cliente OpenAI | paquete `openai` (Node SDK oficial) | Mismo proveedor y mismo patrón que `backend/main.py` (`response_format: { type: "json_object" }`), reutilizando la misma `OPENAI_API_KEY`. |
| Config | `@nestjs/config` con `.env` propio (`backend-nest/.env`, gitignored igual que `backend/.env`) | Aislado del `.env` de Python; evita acoplar ciclos de vida de configuración entre los dos backends. |

## 5. Dockerfile + docker-compose

### `backend-nest/Dockerfile` (multi-stage, Debian, mismo espíritu que `backend/Dockerfile`)

```dockerfile
# caddy:2 es Debian (bookworm) por defecto — se usa solo para copiar el binario.
FROM caddy:2 AS caddy

# node:20-bookworm-slim es Debian 12, no alpine — build stage con devDependencies.
FROM node:20-bookworm-slim AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY tsconfig*.json nest-cli.json ./
COPY src ./src
RUN npm run build

# node:20-bookworm-slim — runtime stage, solo deps de producción.
FROM node:20-bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=caddy /usr/bin/caddy /usr/bin/caddy
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
COPY src/channel-catalog/seed/communities.seed.json ./dist/channel-catalog/seed/communities.seed.json
COPY Caddyfile /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
COPY entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh
EXPOSE 80
ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]
```

`Caddyfile` idéntico en espíritu al de `backend/`, reverse-proxeando `:80 -> 127.0.0.1:3000` (puerto interno Nest). `entrypoint.sh` calca el patrón de `backend/entrypoint.sh` (lanza `node dist/main.js` + `caddy run`, `wait -n`, propagación de señales) — opcionalmente corriendo `npm run migration:run` antes de arrancar Nest.
